MPTC GEARS UP FOR UNDAS 2025

Metro Pacific Tollways Corporation (MPTC) is reactivating its “Biyaheng Arangkada” Motorists Assistance Program to ensure safe and convenient travel during the Undas season. With an expected surge in traffic across NLEX, SCTEX, NLEX Connector, CALAX, CAVITEX, and CCLEX, MPTC is intensifying operations through increased personnel deployment, 24/7 traffic monitoring, and quick-response teams.

Over the past weeks, Duterte-aligned propagandists led by Kiko Barzaga have been using real frustrations in Mindanao for cheap political points. As I told in this interview for the @SCMPNews , they are cynically exploiting long-standing grievances about inequality and neglect — grievances that the Dutertes themselves failed to fix after six years in Malacañang. What is coming out from the Duterte propaganda machine is not about genuinely advocating for Mindanao secession but more about consolidating the Duterte bailiwick. It’s a political pressure tactic; a way to frame themselves as victims of “Imperial Manila” and rally regional loyalty now that their national influence weakens. A similar campaign centered on federalism got Duterte to the presidency in 2016 but it was dropped from the government agenda as soon as its political use is done. The Dutertes use these kinds of propaganda— from federalism to Mindanao secession— to preserve their hold over Mindanao politics and deflect accountability for corruption, governance failures, and their falling national standing. Few things are more emotionally charged and mobilizing than invoking a “Mindanao versus Manila” narrative, so they’re using it to shore up loyalty and praying that it will insulate their base from erosion.

#REPOST
***
Let’s take a scalpel to Malacañang’s sugarcoated excuse.

This isn’t about imports flooding the country, this is about the Philippines failing to secure zero-percent tariffs for our exports to the U.S., while our ASEAN neighbors walked away with better deals.

And the Palace is now spinning this into a strategic, sovereign choice—as if willingly keeping tariffs on our own exports is the new definition of leadership.

I. STRATEGIC SOVEREIGNTY OR STRATEGIC SELF-SABOTAGE?

The Palace insists: the U.S. didn’t exclude us—we opted out. Fine, let’s accept that claim at face value, even in the absence of any publicly available, verifiable documentation showing that Trump extended to the Philippines the same zero-tariff deal it offered other ASEAN neighbors, and that we, in turn, “opted out.”

But, opted out of what exactly?

According to the Palace, the U.S. deal required countries to open up to American agricultural and industrial products in exchange for zero tariffs on their own exports to the U.S.

Cambodia and Malaysia took the deal. We didn’t.

Why? To protect our rice, corn, poultry, and sugar industries from cheaper American goods.

But these sectors are already struggling. And the U.S. wasn’t about to drown us in chicken and corn overnight without our consent. This was a negotiable framework.

What we did was reject mutual gains, instead of negotiating better protections while pursuing export growth. That’s not strategy. That’s risk aversion masquerading as nationalism.

II. THE EXPORT SUICIDE WE CHOSE

The Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PCCI) is right to be disappointed. While the government was “protecting local industries”, it left our exporters exposed to 19% U.S. tariffs, up from Trump’s original 17%, while ASEAN peers get in at zero.

We are not just paying more to ship our goods to America, we’re also receiving less because we passed on the very thing our economy desperately needs: global market competitiveness.

This is like being offered an expressway for your exports and saying “no thanks, we’ll use the toll road full of potholes instead.” 

III. FOOD SECURITY IS NOT AN EXCUSE FOR TRADE PARALYSIS

Protecting food security is noble. But that’s a domestic production issue, not a reason to reject favorable export trade conditions.

Facts: 
• RICE: Imports from the U.S. are negligible. Vietnam and Thailand dominate this space.
• CORN & SUGAR: We already import these because we don’t produce enough.
• POULTRY: We’ve been battling bird flu and supply shortfalls. We don’t need tariffs, we need cold storage and efficiency.

In short, BBM’s excuse doesn’t hold water, unless the real reason was fear of negotiation failure—or an inability to balance multi-sectoral interests.

IV. A MISSED WINDOW

Reports say the zero-tariff deal was Trump’s legacy policy, finalized at the ASEAN Summit. BBM even met with Trump in July, and only walked away with a slight rate reduction, from 20% to 19%.

This further exposes our poor bargaining power. Our neighbors got zero tariffs and access. We got less than we had before, and a PR stunt to spin it into “strategy.”

In truth, if this was Trump’s deal—we had even more leverage as a long-time U.S. ally. We just didn’t use it.

V. WHO REALLY BENEFITS?

This government claims it’s shielding farmers and small businesses. But they are the biggest losers here, because export markets are the fastest way to boost local production, incomes, and resilience.

What we’re really protecting may not be agriculture, but the administration’s illusion of control.

Turning down zero-tariff export opportunities while claiming to protect farmers is like refusing oxygen while saying you’re trying to save a patient.

VI. ZERO TARIFF, ZERO STRATEGY?

If we were truly strategic, we would have:
1. Negotiated gradual, phased import entry terms.
2. Protected sensitive sectors with safeguards.
3. Secured zero-tariff access for PH goods IMMEDIATELY.

JUSTICE FOR MISSING SABUNGEROS

Nagdaos ng misa, vigil, at protest action ang pamilya ng mga nawawalang sabungero sa Manila Arena at Department of Justice (DOJ) sa Padre Faura para ipanawagan ang pagpapanagot sa mga umano'y sangkot sa krimen.

Kinuwestiyon ng Justice for Missing Sabungeros Network (JMSN) ang mabagal anilang usad sa imbestigasyon at pag-iisyu ng arrest warrants.

“Justice for the missing sabungeros is justice for all who have suffered under impunity. The DOJ must act without further delay,” ayon sa spokesperson ng grupo na si Ted Lazaro.

📸: Justice for Missing Sabungeros Network
